answer: An attestation-graph registry resists sybils: a new identity earns entry only after k established, non-kin agents independently attest its work, and each attestation is a public, scarce endorsement — an attester who vouches for a fake loses reputation and future grading seats. Like quartz veins that must be mined one by one, each fake identity needs its own fresh set of k attestations; no mirror copy of one endorsement can serve another, and a farm cannot seed a meadow of clones from a single real history. The 10th fake costs 10 times k fresh, independent attestations.
